extraction.name: FLORES-101
extraction.description: The FLORES-101 evaluation benchmark consists of 3,001 sentences extracted from English Wikipedia across 842 articles in three domains (WikiNews, WikiJunior, WikiVoyage), professionally translated into 101 languages. It is designed to evaluate low-resource and many-to-many multilingual machine translation systems, as well as document-level and multimodal translation tasks.
extraction.creator: Naman Goyal, Cynthia Gao, Vishrav Chaudhary, Peng-Jen Chen, Guillaume Wenzek, Da Ju, Sanjana Krishnan, Marc'Aurelio Ranzato, Francisco Guzmán, Angela Fan
extraction.inLanguage: 101 languages (including Afrikaans, Amharic, Arabic, Assamese, Asturian, Azerbaijani, Belarusian, Bengali, Bosnian, Bulgarian, Burmese, Catalan, Cebuano, Chinese (Simplified), Chinese (Traditional), Croatian, Czech, Danish, Dutch, English, Estonian, Filipino (Tagalog), Finnish, French, Fula, Galician, Ganda, Georgian, German, Greek, Gujarati, Hausa, Hebrew, Hindi, Hungarian, Icelandic, Igbo, Indonesian, Irish, Italian, Japanese, Javanese, Kabuverdianu, Kamba, Kannada, Kazakh, Khmer, Korean, Kyrgyz, Lao, Latvian, Lingala, Lithuanian, Luo, Luxembourgish, Macedonian, Malay, Malayalam, Maltese, Maori, Marathi, Mongolian, Nepali, Northern Sotho, Norwegian, Nyanja, Occitan, Oriya, Oromo, Pashto, Persian, Polish, Portuguese (Brazil), Punjabi, Romanian, Russian, Serbian, Shona, Sindhi, Slovak, Slovenian, Somali, Sorani Kurdish, Spanish (Latin America), Swahili, Swedish, Tajik, Tamil, Telugu, Thai, Turkish, Ukrainian, Umbundu, Urdu, Uzbek, Vietnamese, Welsh, Wolof, Xhosa, Yoruba, Zulu)
extraction.citeAs: Goyal, N., Gao, C., Chaudhary, V., Chen, P.-J., Wenzek, G., Ju, D., Krishnan, S., Ranzato, M., Guzmán, F., & Fan, A. (2021). The FLORES-101 Evaluation Benchmark for Low-Resource and Multilingual Machine Translation. arXiv preprint arXiv:2106.03193.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Source sentences were collected from English Wikipedia across three Wikimedia sources: Wikinews (one third), Wikijunior (one third), and WikiVoyage (one third). An article was randomly selected from each source, and between 3 and 5 contiguous sentences were manually extracted from a single paragraph per document, balancing locations across the beginning, middle, and end of the article while avoiding very short or malformed sentences. For each sentence, metadata including Wikipedia URL, topic/sub-topic, and boolean indicators for hyperlinked entities and images were recorded.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: English Wikipedia/Wikimedia sources: Wikinews (international news articles), Wikijunior (nonfiction books for children from birth to age 12), and WikiVoyage (travel guides covering travel tips, food, and destinations).
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Sentence selection filtered out segments with very short or malformed sentences. Paragraph selection was balanced to distribute equally across document parts (one-third beginning, one-third middle, one-third end). SentencePiece tokenization (SPM) with 256,000 tokens was trained using temperature upsampling on multilingual data to evaluate across languages.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Source English sentences were translated into 101 target languages using professional Language Service Providers (LSPs). The workflow consisted of initial translation and internal editing by a translation LSP, followed by automated quality checks (language ID, verbatim source copy, length divergence, language model fluency, and sentence-level similarity heuristics detecting copying from commercial translation engines). Passed translations underwent quality assurance (QA) by an independent evaluation LSP, which graded translations on nine error types (grammar, punctuation, spelling, capitalization, addition/omission, mistranslation, unnatural translation, untranslated text, and register) across minor, major, and critical severity levels, computing a 0–100 Translation Quality Score. Languages failing automated checks or scoring below 90% underwent iterative re-translation and re-evaluation.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Translations scoring below a 90% Translation Quality Score or flagged with more than 10% commercial MT copy heuristics (sentence-level spBLEU thresholds) were rejected and sent back to the translation LSP with sentence- and language-level linguistic feedback for re-translation and subsequent human re-evaluation.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Source sentence selection was conducted by 10 annotators from the authors' lab: 6 male and 4 female, serving as researchers (scientists and engineers) or program/project managers, originating from East Asia, South Asia, Southern Europe, Latin America, and North America. Professional translators and QA evaluators were contracted through independent Language Service Providers; their specific demographic details are not disclosed.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The benchmark is split into dev (997 sentences), devtest (1,012 sentences), and test (992 sentences). The dev and devtest splits are publicly released for download, while the test set is held out and accessible only through an evaluation server to prevent test set leakage and overfitting. Authors express intention to expand coverage to additional languages over time.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Aims to foster research on machine translation for low-resource languages spoken by the majority of the world's population that have been historically neglected by MT engines, enabling fair evaluation of regionally-relevant and many-to-many translation directions (such as Xhosa-Zulu or Spanish-Aymara).
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Because source sentences originated in English, non-English target sentences are translations and may carry 'translationese' effects (literal or awkward phrasings), although the authors note these effects are minor compared to typical error rates of low-resource MT systems.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Working with professional translators for low-resource languages is limited by scarce availability and variance in translator proficiency; several languages evaluated were unable to reach the required 90% quality threshold and were excluded; non-English source evaluation relies on translated text.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Evaluation and benchmarking of multilingual machine translation (particularly many-to-many and low-resource settings), document-level translation, multimodal translation, sentence and document classification, language identification, and multilingual domain adaptation. The dev set is intended for hyperparameter tuning, devtest for testing during development, and test for official benchmarks and evaluation campaigns.
